Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila) Letter b The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e The principle of legal certainty is the best interest for women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo sanctions imposed jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id - 14 - upon them, or how children will face perpetrators in trial, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.
Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who incidentally is a person they once loved, and so forth. So we as a society or as law enforcement officials need to give opportunities to children and women to express their interests concerning everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAKPAK BHARAT REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's homeland, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) developing the intellectual life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on (a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

Various acts of violence both against women and children inside the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy has the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

Based on that, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community especially to women and children

due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so forth. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of this Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, then handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of prevention and handling of violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in the prevention of violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency.
6. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the grounds of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, such as parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, husbands, wives, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom (local wisdom) is truth that has become traditional or established in an area, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values.

1.9.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Pasal 3(1) indeed states a general aim to “menghapus segala bentuk kekerasan dan eksploitasi terhadap perempuan dan anak,” and Pasal 3(2) lists “kekerasan seksual.” However, the indicator is specifically “Sexual slavery / exploitation.” The regulation does not explicitly mention perbudakan seksual/sexual slavery, sexual exploitation, prostitution, or similar specific forms; “eksploitasi” is generic and appears mainly in the trafficking definition (Pasal 1 angka 7) without specifying sexual exploitation. The judge over-generalized from a broad ‘eliminate exploitation’ objective to a specific sexual-slavery/exploitation category, producing a false positive despite the available passages not supporting that specificity.

2.3.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences discuss establishing service centers, service obligations, performance indicators, and monitoring/evaluation generally, but do not explicitly establish or assign responsibility for a system to collect, record, manage, exchange, or maintain data on violence cases or victims.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 14
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

2.3.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation DOES address an information system explicitly in Pasal 9 ayat (2) huruf e: “membangun dan menyediakan sistem informasi yang lengkap dan mudah diakses.” That is directly relevant to a data/information system indicator. However, the retrieved candidates shown to the judge did not include Pasal 9(2)(e) (they included Pasal 11, 13, 14, 6, etc.), so the judge reasonably answered “No” based on what they saw. This is a retrieval failure rather than a judge reasoning problem.

3.7.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences mention health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, and spiritual guidance, but do not explicitly mention psychosocial or psychological counselling services (e.g., counselling/therapy) as a service for victims.

3.7.rationale: The Indonesian text defines “Pendamping” in Pasal 1 angka 18 as a person/institution representative with expertise to accompany victims to conduct “konseling, terapi dan advokasi” for strengthening and recovery. This is explicit counselling/therapy language (psychosocial support). That definition was present in the retrieved English candidates ([3.7-4]) but the judge focused only on the service lists (health/social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance) and missed that the regulation explicitly includes counselling/therapy via victim accompaniment. Therefore, sufficient evidence was available and the negative verdict reflects judge oversight/over-strictness.

3.10.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions broader prevention efforts such as opening accessibility to training/funding and employment opportunities, the provided sentences do not identify any service unit that provides economic empowerment/support specifically as a victim service unit.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 19
In providing protection to women and children victims of violence, the community may:
a. establish family partners at the village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims;
d. participate with the authorized agencies if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
e. community participation is carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

FUNDING

Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence, is sourced from:

Those passages were retrieved and shown ([3.10-12]). While framed under prevention, they are still government-provided measures enabling funding/income enhancement and employment access, which aligns with economic support/empowerment services. CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 14
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 19
In providing protection to women and children victims of violence, the community may:
a. establish family partners at the village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims;
d. participate with the authorized agencies if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
e. community participation is carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

The judge treated generic rights socialization as equivalent to gender-equality education, which is an overbroad inference given the text. So the false positive stems from evaluation over-inclusiveness.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAKPAK BHARAT REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's homeland, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) developing the intellectual life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on (a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

Various acts of violence both against women and children inside the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy has the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

Based on that, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community especially to women and children

due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so forth. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of this Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, then handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of prevention and handling of violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in the prevention of violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

6.2.rationale: The Indonesian regulation mentions trafficking (“perdagangan orang”) in Pasal 3(1)(a) and defines it in Pasal 1 angka 7, but the operative scope of protection/services throughout is framed for “perempuan dan anak korban kekerasan.” It does not explicitly identify trafficking victims as a distinct intersectional group with tailored measures (e.g., special procedures/services specifically for trafficking victims beyond the general violence-victim framework). The judge inferred that merely mentioning trafficking in objectives/definitions means the policy covers trafficking victims as an intersectional approach. That is too lenient for this indicator, producing a false positive despite the candidates not showing targeted trafficking-victim provisions.
